source_hierarchy: lawful text evidence and evidence-ledger rows

certainty_tags.canon: Directly supported by the novel evidence.
certainty_tags.implied: Strongly supported but not directly stated.
certainty_tags.reconstructed: A practical bridge added to make the structure usable.
certainty_tags.tension: Two supported claims conflict and neither may be silently discarded.

terminology.claim: Project north is a workflow convention until the site directionality is anchored more fully by evidence.
terminology.notes: Do not let project north become false canon.

claims.notes: Treat the keep as a primary structural anchor.

claims.claim: Castle Crydee has walls and towers as active defensive elements.
claims.notes: Do not downplay the castle shell into an unfortified manor.

claims.claim: The castle and the town below are distinct settlement levels or zones.
claims.notes: Do not flatten the castle and lower town into one level plane.

claims.claim: The great hall is a major public-noble room where the Duke holds court.
claims.notes: This is one of the safest interior anchors.

claims.claim: A courtyard gate and courtyard movement sequence are part of the castle approach.
claims.notes: Preserve circulation logic instead of inventing ornamental forecourts.

claims.claim: A long corridor connects the kitchen and the great hall.
claims.notes: This service route should shape interior planning.

claims.claim: Castle Crydee has a west wall and battlements.
claims.notes: Preserve this directional anchor once more site references are gathered.

claims.claim: Do not treat Castle Crydee as a neat concentric super-castle without evidence.
Do not merge peacetime and siege-state layout assumptions into one false definitive map.
claims.notes: Version major state changes if needed later.

validation_rules.notes: Keep the strongest elevation clue alive when prompts mention the settlement.
